geographic_scope: Jammu & Kashmir (Doda, Bhaderwah, Kishtwar, Udhampur, Kathua, Reasi, Ramban)
variety_coverage: Western Pahari and tribal speech varieties of Jammu mountains (including Gaddi communities settled in Jammu)
relevant_pages: Vol. 1: Survey & structural analysis of hill dialects; tribal and caste dialects chapter (Gaddi, Gojri, Bakerwali, Watali, Cinnali). Vol. 2: Source materials, Padri/Bhalesi texts, Glossary of Cinali (confirmed: lacks Gaddi vocabulary). Google Books (id=pHZOAQAAIAAJ) exposes only fragmentary, unverified TOC strings ('Preface', 'Fundamentals of Jammus Linguistics 1844', 'and verb forms', '7 other sections not shown'); no actual scanned page images are viewable.

evidence_evaluation: Publisher, national library, and international catalogue records verify that Vol. 1 was published by Eastern Book Linkers (Delhi, 2006) as the outcome of a UGC Major Research Project on Jammu Pahari and tribal dialects. Google Books maintains a catalogued bibliographic record with snippet-level indexing (id=pHZOAQAAIAAJ, Volume 1). However, the platform exposes no actual scanned page images or eBook download ('Snippet view', 'No eBook available'), and the service does not specify the legal or contractual reason for restricted viewability. Extracted TOC text is fragmentary and contains unverified parsing/OCR artifacts ('Fundamentals of Jammus Linguistics 1844', 'and verb forms'). Crucially, no Gaddi linguistic text, wordlists, or grammatical paradigms can be viewed online. Vol. 2's specific glossaries cover Cinali (Chinali) and studies on Padri/Bhalesi; Vol. 2 does NOT contain a dedicated Gaddi vocabulary. Volume 1 contents cannot be inferred from Volume 2. Physical holdings at Dhanvantri Central Library (Jammu), Sahitya Akademi (New Delhi), National Library (Kolkata), and Library of Congress have not been confirmed by direct shelf inspection and remain classified as institutional_confirmation_required.

title: Jambu Gaddi Lexical Dataset (1,118 Forms)
variety_coverage: Himachal Pradesh Gaddi (Bharmaur, Chamba and Kangra reflexes in CDIAL)
relevant_pages: Web interface at neojambu.herokuapp.com/languages/ga; derived from Turner (1966) CDIAL entries citing 'G.'
page_or_section: Entire Gaddi language slice in Jambu (1,118 lexemes)
license_or_rights: Application MIT / Underlying CDIAL etymological data copyright ? Oxford University Press / SOAS London
evidence_evaluation: The Jambu project implements a Cross-Linguistic Data Format (CLDF) export of Sir Ralph Lilley Turner's Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages (CDIAL, 1966). Jambu indexes 1,118 forms tagged as Gaddi ('ga'). An audit of the underlying sources reveals that Turner compiled these forms citing 'G.' exclusively from Rev. T. Grahame Bailey (1908, The Languages of the Northern Himalayas, Chamba and Kangra Gaddi) and Sir George A. Grierson (1916, LSI Vol. IX Part IV, Brahmaur Gadi). Jambu explicitly maps the language to coordinates 32.36, 76.57 (Bharmaur, Chamba, Himachal Pradesh). EXACTLY ZERO of the 1,118 forms originate from Jammu & Kashmir. Quarantined as comparative_only to prevent conflation with J&K Gaddi.
verification_notes: PROVENANCE AUDIT: 1,118 headwords in Jambu represent 100% Himachal Pradesh historical data (Bharmaur/Kangra via Turner CDIAL 1966, Bailey 1908, Grierson 1916). No field or written citations from J&K (Doda, Bhaderwah, Kathua, Udhampur). Confirmed zero J&K provenance. Quarantined under comparative_only.
actionable_next_steps: Retain as historical comparative dataset for Indo-Aryan cognate tracing; strictly bar from verified_jk_lexical_entries.
